text:
Predicates:
InCity(x, y) ::: x is in city y.
InState(x, y) ::: x is in state y.
City(x) ::: x is a city.
State(x) ::: x is a state.
InSameState(x, y) ::: x and y are in the same state.
DifferentStates(x, y) ::: x and y are in different states.
UniqueState(x) ::: x is in only one state.
Premises:
City(Billings) ∧ State(Montana) ∧ InCity(Billings, Montana) ::: Billings is a city in Montana.
State(Montana) ∧ City(Butte) ∧ City(Helena) ∧ City(Missoula) ::: Montana includes Butte, Helena, Missoula.
InCity(WhiteSulphurSprings, Montana) ∧ InCity(Butte, Montana) ::: White Sulphur Springs and Butte are cities in Montana.
¬InCity(StPierre, Montana) ::: St Pierre is not in Montana.
∀x (InCity(x, Butte) → ¬InCity(x, StPierre)) ::: Any city in Butte is not in St Pierre.
∀x, y (InCity(x, y) ∧ City(x) ∧ City(y) → (InSameState(x, y) ∨ DifferentStates(x, y))) ::: A city can only be in one state, except for specified exceptions.
Conclusion:
InSameState(StPierre, Bismarck) ::: St Pierre and Bismarck are in the same state.
